mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-01.title: Area of each wall
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-01.body:
Paintable height: $8 - 0.5 = 7.5$ ft.
- 12-ft wall: $12 \times 7.5 - 5 \times 6 = 90 - 30 = 60$ ft².
- 9-ft wall: $9 \times 7.5 = 67.5$ ft².

Total $127.5$ ft², four coats: $510$ ft². Paint: $510 \div 400 = 1.275 \approx 1.28$ gallons.

**Answer: 1.28 gallons**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-01.title: Both walls together
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-01.body:
The two walls are $12 + 9 = 21$ ft wide, so without the baseboard they have $21 \times 7.5 = 157.5$ ft²; minus the 30-ft² window gives $127.5$ ft². Four coats is $4 \times 127.5 \div 400 = 1.275$ gallons ≈ 1.28.

**Answer: 1.28 gallons**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-02.title: Find each amount
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-02.body:
There are $4 + 9 + 2 = 15$ parts, so each part is $3 \div 15 = 0.2$ pint. Magenta: $4(0.2) = 0.8$; yellow: $9(0.2) = 1.8$. Difference: $1$ pint.

**Answer: 1 pint**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-02.title: Difference in parts
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-02.body:
Yellow has $9 - 4 = 5$ more parts than magenta, which is $\frac{5}{15} = \frac13$ of the mixture: $\frac13 \times 3 = 1$ pint.

**Answer: 1 pint**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-03.title: Yellow in two places
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-03.body:
Total parts: $2 + 1 + 5 + 10 = 18$.
- Yellow directly: $\frac{5}{18} \times 2 = \frac59$ gallon.
- Light green: $\frac{10}{18} \times 2 = \frac{10}{9}$ gallons, of which $\frac{14}{15}$ is yellow: $\frac{14}{15} \times \frac{10}{9} = \frac{28}{27}$ gallon.

Total yellow: $\frac{15}{27} + \frac{28}{27} = \frac{43}{27} = 1\frac{16}{27}$ gallons.

**Answer: $1\frac{16}{27}$ gallons**

mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-03.title: Rewrite the recipe with 15ths
mathcounts-potw-2026-03-23-03.body:
Split each of the 10 light-green parts into 15 sub-parts: light green = 150 sub-parts = 140 yellow + 10 green. Scaling the other colors by 15: white 30, red 15, yellow 75. Total $30 + 15 + 75 + 150 = 270$ sub-parts, of which yellow is $75 + 140 = 215$. Yellow $= \frac{215}{270} \times 2 = \frac{43}{27} = 1\frac{16}{27}$ gallons.

**Answer: $1\frac{16}{27}$ gallons**
